\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.Programs.Light.Lib.ArrayAt}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[A list on a segment]
\lean{Light.ListAt}
\label{Light.ListAt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Seg}
A list of integers is located at index $a$ in a function from natural numbers to
integers, with length $N$ and upper limit $top$, if its length is $N$, its entries agree
with the function on the consecutive indices from $a$ through $a+N-1$, and $a+N\le top$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[A bounded list on a segment]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt}
\label{Light.ArrayAt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.AbsLe, Light.Seg}
A list of integers is located at index $a$ in a function from natural numbers to
integers, with length $N$, absolute-value bound $U$, and upper limit $top$, if its
length is $N$, its entries agree with the function on the consecutive indices starting
at $a$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and $a+N\le top$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Preserving a recorded list under agreement]
\lean{Light.ListAt.keep}
\label{Light.ListAt.keep}
\leanok
\uses{Light.Inside, Light.ListAt, Light.SameOn, Light.Seg.congr}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and suppose a list $l$ of length $N$ records the
values of $\mu$ at the consecutive indices starting at $a$, where $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$.
If $\mu'$ agrees with $\mu$ at every index $b$ satisfying $a\le b<a+N$ and
$b<\mathrm{top}$, then $l$ also records $\mu'$ on that segment, with the same length and
bound.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of the upper bound]
\lean{Light.ListAt.mono}
\label{Light.ListAt.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ListAt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and suppose a list $l$ of length $N$ records the values
of $\mu$ at the consecutive indices starting at $a$, with $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. For any
$\mathrm{top}'$ with $\mathrm{top}\le\mathrm{top}'$, the same list records the same
segment and satisfies $a+N\le\mathrm{top}'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reading a recorded list entry]
\lean{Light.ListAt.read}
\label{Light.ListAt.read}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ListAt, Light.Seg.getD}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and suppose a list $l$ of length $N$ records the values
of $\mu$ at the consecutive indices starting at $a$, with $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. For
every $i<N$, the value $\mu(a+i)$ equals the list entry at index $i$; equivalently, it
equals the default-zero lookup of $l$ at $i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restricting a list segment]
\lean{Light.ListAt.drop_take}
\label{Light.ListAt.drop_take}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ListAt, Light.Seg.drop, Light.Seg.take}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$, and suppose a list $l$ of length $N$ records the values
of $\mu$ on the consecutive indices starting at $a$, with $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. For
natural numbers $k,n$ with $k+n\le N$, the list obtained by dropping the first $k$
entries of $l$ and taking the next $n$ entries has length $n$, records $\mu$ starting at
$a+k$, and satisfies $a+k+n\le\mathrm{top}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An Array Specification Gives a List Specification]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.listAt}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.listAt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ArrayAt, Light.ListAt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,N,\mathrm{top}\in\mathbb{N}$, $l$ be a list of
integers, and $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. If $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is $\mu(a+j)$ for
every $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$, then
$l$ has length $N$, records those values of $\mu$, and satisfies $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preservation Under Agreement on the Interval]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.keep}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.keep}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ArrayAt, Light.ArrayAt.listAt, Light.Inside, Light.ListAt.keep, Light.SameOn}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,N,\mathrm{top}\in\mathbb{N}$, $l$ be a list
of integers, and $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is
$\mu(a+j)$ for each $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. Suppose also that $\mu'(b)=\mu(b)$ whenever $a\le b<a+N$ and
$b<\mathrm{top}$. Then the same list satisfies these array conditions for $\mu'$ with
the same $a,N,U,\mathrm{top}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of Array Bounds and Endpoint]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.mono}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.mono}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ArrayAt}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,N,\mathrm{top},\mathrm{top}'\in\mathbb{N}$, $l$ be
a list of integers, and $U,U'\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry
is $\mu(a+j)$ for each $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. If $U\le U'$ and $\mathrm{top}\le\mathrm{top}'$, then the same
list satisfies the array conditions with bound $U'$ and endpoint $\mathrm{top}'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reading an Array Entry]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.read}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.read}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ArrayAt, Light.ArrayAt.listAt, Light.ListAt.read}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,N,\mathrm{top},i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $l$ be a list
of integers, and let $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is
$\mu(a+j)$ for every $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. Then the value $\mu(a+i)$ equals the $i$th entry of $l$ when
$i<N$; equivalently, it equals the default value $0$ if that index is out of range.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on an Array Read]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.abs_read_le}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.abs_read_le}
\leanok
\uses{Light.AbsLe.getElem, Light.ArrayAt}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,\mathrm{top},i\in\mathbb{N}$, let $l$ be a
list of integers, and let $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry
is $\mu(a+j)$ for every $j<N$, every entry $x$ of $l$ satisfies $|x|\le U$, and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. Then $|\mu(a+i)|\le U$ whenever $i<N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Specification of a Subarray]
\lean{Light.ArrayAt.drop_take}
\label{Light.ArrayAt.drop_take}
\leanok
\uses{Light.ArrayAt, Light.ArrayAt.listAt, Light.ListAt.drop_take}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, $a,k,n,\mathrm{top}\in\mathbb{N}$, $l$ be a list of
integers, and $U\in\mathbb{Z}$. Suppose $l$ has length $N$, its $j$th entry is
$\mu(a+j)$ for each $j<N$, every entry has absolute value at most $U$, and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. If $k+n\le N$, then the list obtained by dropping the first $k$
entries of $l$ and taking the next $n$ entries has length $n$, records the values of
$\mu$ starting at index $a+k$, has all entries bounded in absolute value by $U$, and
satisfies $(a+k)+n\le\mathrm{top}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[A bounded-index list on a segment]
\lean{Light.IndexAt}
\label{Light.IndexAt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.SegN}
A list of natural numbers is located at index $a$ in a function from natural numbers to
integers, with length $N$, value bound $p$, and upper limit $top$, if its length is $N$,
its entries agree with the function on the consecutive indices starting at $a$ (after
viewing each list entry as an integer), every entry is strictly less than $p$, and
$a+N\le top$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Preserving an indexed segment]
\lean{Light.IndexAt.keep}
\label{Light.IndexAt.keep}
\leanok
\uses{Light.IndexAt, Light.Inside, Light.SameOn, Light.Seg.congr}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu,\mu':\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$ be natural numbers, and
let $l$ be a list of natural numbers of length $N$. Suppose its entries agree with
$\mu(a+i)$ for $0\le i<N$ (after viewing each entry as an integer), every entry is less
than $p$, and $a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. If $\mu$ and $\mu'$ agree at every natural number
$b$ satisfying $a\le b<a+N$ and $b<\mathrm{top}$, then the same list also has these
properties as an indexed segment for $\mu'$, with the same $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reading an indexed segment]
\lean{Light.IndexAt.read}
\label{Light.IndexAt.read}
\leanok
\uses{Light.IndexAt, Light.SegN.read}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$ be natural numbers, and let
$l$ be a natural-number list of length $N$ whose entries agree with $\mu(a+i)$ for $0\le
i<N$ (after viewing each entry as an integer), with every entry less than $p$ and
$a+N\le\mathrm{top}$. For every $i<N$, $\mu(a+i)$ equals the list entry at index $i$,
using $0$ as the default when the index is out of range, viewed as an integer.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on a list entry]
\lean{Light.IndexAt.getD_lt}
\label{Light.IndexAt.getD_lt}
\leanok
\uses{Light.IndexAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$, let $a,N,p,\mathrm{top}$ be natural numbers, and let
$l$ be a list of natural numbers such that its length is $N$, its entries agree with
$\mu(a+i)$ for $0\le i<N$ (after viewing each entry as an integer), every entry is less
than $p$, and $a+N\le \mathrm{top}$. For every $i<N$, the entry of $l$ at index $i$,
using $0$ as the default when the index is out of range, is less than $p$.
\end{theorem}
